title: Rejection policies
context: What are the rejection policies of ThreadPoolExecutor?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: AbortPolicy, the default, throws RejectedExecutionException. CallerRunsPolicy runs the task on the caller's thread, which slows submission and gives natural back-pressure. DiscardPolicy silently drops the new task. DiscardOldestPolicy drops the oldest queued task and retries the new one. You can also write your own handler, for example to log the task or write it to a durable queue. Pick one on purpose: silent drops hide load problems.

points.title: Default throws
points.why: AbortPolicy throws, so callers must handle the exception.

points.title: Back-pressure
points.why: CallerRunsPolicy slows the submitter instead of losing work.
